shared_context.content: For integers A,B,d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q_{A,B,d}(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)); when d = 0 the empty product is 1.
shared_context.label: Q_{A,B,d}(q)

shared_context.content: Write w_j := B+j for j=1,...,d and e_i := A+i for i=1,...,d.
shared_context.label: Weights and target degrees

shared_context.content: For J subseteq {1,...,d}, define Sigma(J) := {sum_{j in J} m_j w_j : each m_j is a nonnegative integer}. Thus Sigma(J) is the set of weighted degrees occurring in the coordinate subring generated by variables with indices in J.
shared_context.label: Numerical semigroup attached to a subset of variables

shared_context.content: For a positively graded Q-algebra R = direct_sum_{n >= 0} R_n, write Hilb_R(q) := sum_{n >= 0} (dim_Q R_n) q^n.
shared_context.label: Hilbert series

strategy_summary: Use a two-stage existence theorem. First translate polynomiality of Q_{A,B,d}(q) into divisibility inequalities via cyclotomic factor multiplicities, then into a Hall-type condition on which target degrees are visible on each coordinate subspace of the weighted affine space. Next invoke a weighted complete-intersection realization theorem: if every coordinate stratum sees enough accessible degrees, then one can choose homogeneous forms of the prescribed degrees whose only common zero is the origin. From there, Nullstellensatz gives an Artinian quotient, Cohen-Macaulayness upgrades it to a regular sequence, and the Hilbert-series formula yields Q_{A,B,d}(q).
